situation:
You are the financial analyst at BRACKWELL TOOLWORKS, a mid-size manufacturer of hand tools and workbench hardware. The founder (judge), who started the company thirty years ago and is preparing to hand it to a new owner at the end of the year, has asked you to recommend how the company should sell to its customers online.

BRACKWELL TOOLWORKS is profitable and moves most of its volume through hardware chains, but its fastest growth has come from the small online storefront it built itself. That storefront records what each customer buys and when a tool comes back for service, and the company has spent two years and a great deal of capital building a paid maintenance subscription on top of those purchase records.

PELLWORTH MARKETPLACE, a national online retail platform, has offered a three-year agreement that would list every BRACKWELL product to millions of shoppers. Signing the three-year agreement lifts reported revenue in time for the closing quarter the founder's sale price is measured on, and it hands PELLWORTH MARKETPLACE control of pricing and of the customer purchase records the maintenance subscription reads.

Declining the platform and finishing the in-house storefront keeps the purchase records and the subscription in the company's own hands, and it returns nothing on the capital already spent until the third year, leaving the closing quarter short of the revenue the founder has told the buyer to expect. The buyer will see whichever set of numbers the company reports, and will read them as the founder's own account of the business.

The founder (judge) wants your analysis of the return each course of action earns on the capital it uses, a view on what the purchase records are worth beyond the accounting they were kept for, and a recommendation on which way the company should go. The founder (judge) will greet you and ask to hear your ideas, and will thank you after your presentation and questions.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the founder (judge) of BRACKWELL TOOLWORKS. Business background is the same as the situation above.

You want the participant to analyze the return each course of action earns on the capital it uses, to say what the storefront's purchase records are worth beyond the accounting they were kept for, and to recommend whether the company signs the three-year agreement with PELLWORTH MARKETPLACE or finishes the storefront it built itself.
